title: `asdict(self.split_config) if self.split_config else {}` — the `else {}` branch is unreachable and contradicts the unconditional `self.split_config.<attr>` access 17 lines below in the same call
description: In `_log_to_mlflow`, the `metadata = ModelCardMetadata(...)` construction guards the split_config field with `split_config=asdict(self.split_config) if self.split_config else {}`. `self.split_config` is assigned unconditionally in `__init__` (lines 358-363): it is always a `SplitConfig` — a passed `SplitConfig`, a `SplitConfig(**split)` built from a dict, or `SplitConfig()` — and is never `None`. `SplitConfig` is a plain `@dataclass` (src/haute/modelling/_split.py:12-13) with no `__bool__` or `__len__`, so any instance is always truthy. The `else {}` branch is therefore dead. Worse, it is internally inconsistent: the very same `log_experiment(...)` call dereferences `self.split_config` WITHOUT any guard at lines 1568-1570 (`self.split_config.strategy`, `self.split_config.validation_size`, `self.split_config.holdout_size`). If `self.split_config` could ever be falsy/None (the premise of the line-1551 guard), those three accesses would raise `AttributeError` first — proving the guard is both unnecessary and contradictory. The simplification is to drop the guard: `split_config=asdict(self.split_config)`.
evidence: __init__ lines 358-363: `if isinstance(split, SplitConfig): self.split_config = split / elif isinstance(split, dict): self.split_config = SplitConfig(**split) / else: self.split_config = SplitConfig()` — every branch sets a SplitConfig, none sets None. _split.py:12-13 shows `@dataclass\nclass SplitConfig:` with no __bool__/__len__ override (grep found none) ⇒ always truthy. Same method, line 1551 guards it, while lines 1568-1570 inside the immediately-following `log_experiment(...)` call read `self.split_config.strategy / .validation_size / .holdout_size` unconditionally. The guarded and unguarded usages cannot both be correct; the unguarded ones are correct, so the guard is dead.
est_reduction: -0 to -1 LOC (replace `asdict(self.split_config) if self.split_config else {}` with `asdict(self.split_config)`); removes one dead branch and the false implication that split_config can be None.
behavior_preservation: Behaviour-identical for all reachable states: self.split_config is always a truthy SplitConfig, so the expression already always evaluates to `asdict(self.split_config)`. No call path can make the `else {}` fire (run() is the only caller of _log_to_mlflow and it uses the same self instance whose __init__ guaranteed a SplitConfig).
